10 Iddhibaladassanapañha 10. Question on the Display of Psychic Power

“Bhante nāgasena, bhāsitampetaṁ bhagavatā—“Venerable Nāgasena, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṁ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṁ vā’ti. ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed by the Tathāgata, made much of, made a vehicle, made a ground, established, consolidated, and well undertaken. If he wished, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could live for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon.’ Puna ca bhaṇitaṁ—And again it was said: ‘ito tiṇṇaṁ māsānaṁ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’ti. ‘At the end of three months from now the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna.’ Yadi, bhante nāgasena, bhagavatā bhaṇitaṁ—If, venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said, ‘tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā …pe… kappāvasesaṁ vā’ti, tena hi temāsaparicchedo micchā. ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed by the Tathāgata ... or for the remainder of an aeon,’ then the fixing of the limit at three months is false. Yadi, bhante, tathāgatena bhaṇitaṁ—If, venerable sir, the Tathāgata said, ‘ito tiṇṇaṁ māsānaṁ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’ti, tena hi ‘tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā …pe… kappāvasesaṁ vā’ti tampi vacanaṁ micchā. ‘At the end of three months from now the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna,’ then the statement ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed ... or for the remainder of an aeon’ is also false. Natthi tathāgatānaṁ aṭṭhāne gajjitaṁ. There is no roaring (empty boasting) by the Tathāgatas about what is impossible. Amoghavacanā buddhā bhagavanto tathavacanā advejjhavacanā. The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are of efficacious speech, of true speech, of speech without duplicity. Ayampi ubhato koṭiko pañho gambhīro sunipuṇo dunnijjhāpayo tavānuppatto, bhindetaṁ diṭṭhijālaṁ, ekaṁse ṭhapaya, bhinda paravādan”ti. This double-pronged dilemma is profound, very subtle, and hard to understand; it has now come to you. Break this net of views, set it down on one side, and shatter the doctrines of opponents.”

“Bhāsitampetaṁ, mahārāja, bhagavatā ‘tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā …pe… kappāvasesaṁ vā’ti, temāsaparicchedo ca bhaṇito, so ca pana kappo āyukappo vuccati. “Your majesty, this was spoken by the Blessed One: ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed ... or for the remainder of an aeon,’ and the limit of three months was also stated. But that ‘aeon’ (kappa) is called the aeon of a life-span (āyukappa). Na, mahārāja, bhagavā attano balaṁ kittayamāno evamāha, iddhibalaṁ pana, mahārāja, bhagavā parikittayamāno evamāha—The Blessed One, your majesty, did not speak thus in proclaiming his own strength; rather, in declaring the power of psychic ability, the Blessed One spoke thus: ‘tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā …pe… kappāvasesaṁ vā’ti. ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed ... or for the remainder of an aeon.’

Yathā, mahārāja, rañño assājānīyo bhaveyya sīghagati anilajavo, tassa rājā javabalaṁ parikittayanto sanegamajānapadabhaṭabalabrāhmaṇagahapatikaamaccajanamajjhe evaṁ vadeyya ‘ākaṅkhamāno me, bho, ayaṁ hayavaro sāgarajalapariyantaṁ mahiṁ anuvicaritvā khaṇena idhāgaccheyyā’ti, na ca taṁ javagatiṁ tassaṁ parisāyaṁ dasseyya, vijjati ca so javo tassa, samattho ca so khaṇena sāgarajalapariyantaṁ mahiṁ anuvicarituṁ. Suppose, your majesty, a king had a thoroughbred horse, swift in gait, with the speed of the wind. In declaring that horse’s strength of speed, in the midst of townspeople, country people, soldiers, brahmins, householders, and ministers, the king might say: ‘If I wished, sirs, this excellent horse could roam the earth bounded by the ocean’s waters and come back here in an instant.’ Yet he would not display that speed in that assembly, though the speed exists in the horse, and it is capable of roaming the earth bounded by the ocean in an instant. Evameva kho, mahārāja, bhagavā attano iddhibalaṁ parikittayamāno evamāha, tampi tevijjānaṁ chaḷabhiññānaṁ arahantānaṁ vimalakhīṇāsavānaṁ devamanussānañca majjhe nisīditvā bhaṇitaṁ—In the same way, your majesty, the Blessed One spoke thus in declaring his own psychic power, and he said it while seated in the midst of arahants with the three knowledges and the six direct knowledges, stainless, their taints destroyed, and in the middle of devas and humans: ‘tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṁ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṁ vā’ti. ‘The four bases of psychic power, Ānanda, have been developed by the Tathāgata ... If he wished, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could live for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon.’ Vijjati ca taṁ, mahārāja, iddhibalaṁ bhagavato, samattho ca bhagavā iddhibalena kappaṁ vā ṭhātuṁ kappāvasesaṁ vā, na ca bhagavā taṁ iddhibalaṁ tassaṁ parisāyaṁ dasseti, anatthiko, mahārāja, bhagavā sabbabhavehi, garahitā ca tathāgatassa sabbabhavā. That psychic power, your majesty, does exist in the Blessed One, and the Blessed One is capable by psychic power of staying for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon. But the Blessed One does not display that psychic power in that assembly, for the Blessed One, your majesty, has no need of any kind of existence, and all existence is condemned by the Tathāgata. Bhāsitampetaṁ, mahārāja, bhagavatā—This too was spoken by the Blessed One, your majesty: ‘seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, appamattakopi gūtho duggandho hoti; ‘Just as, bhikkhus, even a tiny bit of excrement stinks, evameva kho ahaṁ, bhikkhave, appamattakampi bhavaṁ na vaṇṇemi antamaso accharāsaṅghātamattampī’ti api nu kho, mahārāja, bhagavā sabbabhavagatiyoniyo gūthasamaṁ disvā iddhibalaṁ nissāya bhavesu chandarāgaṁ kareyyā”ti? in the same way, bhikkhus, I do not praise even a tiny bit of existence, even for as long as a finger-snap.’ Would the Blessed One, your majesty, seeing all existences, destinies, and modes of birth as like excrement, rely on psychic power and generate desire and lust for existences?” “Na hi, bhante”ti. “Certainly not, venerable sir.” “Tena hi, mahārāja, bhagavā iddhibalaṁ parikittayamāno evarūpaṁ buddhasīhanādamabhinadī”ti. “Then, your majesty, in proclaiming his psychic power, the Blessed One gave voice to such a lion’s roar as of a Buddha.” “Sādhu, bhante nāgasena, evametaṁ tathā sampaṭicchāmī”ti. “Very good, venerable Nāgasena. I accept it as you say.”

Iddhibaladassanapañho dasamo. Question on the Display of Psychic Power tenth
